correctness.rationale: For any nonedge {u,v}, diameter≤2 and no 4-cycle give a unique common neighbor w; triangle-freeness ensures uw,vw are edges and uv is the only nonedge of {u,v,w}. The Δ2 facet F_uv=V ∖ {u,v} has free codimension-one face σ_uv=V ∖ {u,v,w}, because any other Δ2 facet containing σ would come from a nonedge in {u,v,w}; there is none. Distinct nonedges yield distinct σ, so all pairs may be removed sequentially. Every disconnected triple contains a nonedge, hence Δ3⊆Δ2. Every remaining face τ of Δ2 has complement X containing a nonedge uv: if |X|=2 it was a removed facet; if |X|=3 then either X={u,v,w} was a removed σ or X induces a disconnected triple; if |X|≥4 choose x∈X\{u,v,w}, so {u,v,x} is disconnected and τ is a Δ3 face. Thus the remainder is exactly Δ3, proving an elementary simplicial collapse for all stated graphs, not only a homotopy equivalence. For connected triangle-free G, Bayer et al., Theorem 6.4 and Corollary 6.3, give Δ2≃∨^{e−n+1}S^{n−4}, with zero interpreted contractibly; Petersen has (n,e)=(10,15), hence six 6-spheres. Separate independent enumeration of all 2^10 and 2^15 labeled graphs yields exactly 17 qualifying n=5 graphs and 6 qualifying n=6 graphs, and verifies the collapse pair set in every case. Direct Petersen enumeration gives f(Δ2)=(10,45,120,210,252,210,120,30), f(Δ3)=(10,45,120,210,252,210,90) and 30 distinct collapse pairs.

Under unique common neighbors, Σ_v binom(deg v,2)=binom(n,2)−e, hence that formula gives e−n+1 spheres for all n≥7 cases here; the published same-day result already covers the wedge and Petersen homotopy consequences.

originality.rationale: The original mathematical contribution is the explicit global simplicial collapse Δ2(G)↘Δ3(G) under unique common neighbors; exact facet/free-face bijection and residual-complex identification. Bayer et al. (2024) provides the Δ2 wedge and Petersen Δ2 result but not this collapse. Important correction to the package's own originality discussion: the separately published same-day Resultary/SCOPE record --868c7d2aa0e7 proves a much broader Δ3 wedge theorem and signed character formula, which specializes to the sphere count here via Σ_v binom(deg v,2)=binom(n,2)−e. Therefore the Δ3 homotopy formula and Petersen six-sphere corollary are mathematically covered, not separately novel. The stronger source collapses Δ3's Alexander dual, not the actual inclusion Δ3⊂Δ2; neither equal homotopy types nor a dual-collapse prove a simplicial collapse of the inclusion. Nearby publications on squared cycles and powers do not contain this structural inclusion theorem. PASS is limited to the nontrivial surviving structural bridge, not the already covered corollary.

scope_of_result: For finite connected triangle-free and four-cycle-free diameter-at-most-two graphs on n≥5 vertices, Δ2 collapses simplicially onto Δ3; known general Δ2 results supply its homotopy type. The independently known broader Δ3 formula covers the resulting wedge statement for n≥7.

value.rationale: A canonical elementary-collapse relation between two natural cut-complex parameters is a substantive combinatorial-topology structural lemma. It identifies a free face for every Δ2 facet using a graph-theoretic local uniqueness law and proves the inclusion Δ3⊂Δ2 is a simple-homotopy equivalence, a finer result than the already known individual wedge types; it supplies an explicit collapse sequence useful for relative topology, functorial comparisons and concrete computations. The diameter-two, triangle- and four-cycle-free hypothesis is motivated by Moore graphs and stars (including C5, Petersen, Hoffman–Singleton), not an arbitrary small slice. The proof isolates the precise multiple-common-neighbor obstruction. Value does not rest on claiming novelty of the six-sphere count, which is covered by the broader same-day three-cut theorem, or on the finite script.
